content.text: {"answers": [{"question_id": "Q1", "question": "What event or signal starts the review — for example, does the engineer receive an automated notification, a manual assignment in a task system, or an email — and where does the specification document come from at that moment?", "answer": "Something typically triggers it — maybe a notification or just someone passing it along. The document comes from wherever it usually lives, more or less."}, {"question_id": "Q2", "question": "What specific criteria or checklist does the engineer use to decide whether a new feature is correctly reflected in the document?", "answer": "There is generally some kind of reference the reviewer looks at, though the exact criteria can vary depending on the situation."}, {"question_id": "Q3", "question": "Can you walk me through the sequence of individual steps the engineer performs during the review, from opening the document to completing it?", "answer": "The person in charge usually looks things over, checks for issues, notes anything off, and passes it along when done."}, {"question_id": "Q4", "question": "What are the possible outcomes at the end of the review, and what action or next step does each outcome trigger?", "answer": "It either moves forward or goes back for more work, depending on whether things look acceptable or not."}, {"question_id": "Q5", "question": "Which tools or systems does the engineer use during the review, and in what file format is the specification document typically stored?", "answer": "Some tools are involved for viewing and commenting, and the document is stored in a common format somewhere accessible."}, {"question_id": "Q6", "question": "After the engineer completes the review, who receives the document or the review findings, and does any other role participate in the process before or after the engineer's review?", "answer": "Others are generally involved before and after — someone hands it off, and someone else handles it once the review wraps up."}]}
